detail.longDescription: I have a custom build profile named custom-release , which inherits the release build profile and also sets some extra flags. However when I try to access the build profile via the environment variable PROFILE in the build script build.rs it shows as release instead of custom-release . Is this the intended behavior or something is wrong in here? Cargo.toml [package] name = "build_profile" version = "0.1.0" edition = "2024" [profile.release] opt-level = 2 lto = true [profile.custom-release] inherits = "release" lto = false [build-dependencies] build-print = "1.0.1" [dependencies] build.rs use std::env; use build_print::println; fn main() { let profile = env::var("PROFILE").unwrap_or_default(); println!("build profile: {profile}"); } src/main.rs fn main() { println!("Hello, world!"); } cargo command cargo build --profile release output Compiling build-print v1.0.1 Compiling build_profile v0.1.0 (/home/harsha/build_profile) build profile: release Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 2.42s cargo command cargo build --profile custom-release current output Compiling build-print v1.0.1 Compiling build_profile v0.1.0 (/home/harsha/build_profile) build profile: release Finished `custom-release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 0.27s cargo command cargo build --profile custom-release expected output Compiling build-print v1.0.1 Compiling build_profile v0.1.0 (/home/harsha/build_profile) build profile: custom-release Finished `custom-release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 0.27s
